sentences.label: Lowering the risk
sentences.text: These add up independently, and these lower the risk: through this sum alone, compared with no chest pain symptoms, typical angina takes a typical patient's predicted risk from about 20% to below 1%, non-anginal chest pain to about 1% and atypical angina to about 6%; being a woman lowers it to about 1% and fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL to about 3%, and a higher maximum heart rate lowers it steadily, from about 32% at 118 to about 14% at 175 beats per minute; chest pain type, sex and fasting blood sugar also act through the parts below.

sentences.label: Raising the risk
sentences.text: A flat rather than upsloping ST segment raises it to about 90%, and higher cholesterol (from about 8% at 193 mg/dL to about 53% at 308 mg/dL), higher resting blood pressure (from about 11% at 110 mm Hg to about 36% at 155 mm Hg) and older age (from about 15% at 42 to about 23% at 66 years) raise it steadily.

Through this sum alone, each extra vessel coloured by fluoroscopy adds about the same, from about 20% at 0 to about 96% at 2 vessels, flattening out near the top because the predicted risk cannot go much higher, and a reversible defect on the thallium scan, compared with any other thallium result, raises it to about 39%; both also act through the parts below.

sentences.label: Rare results
sentences.text: A downsloping ST segment raises it to about 40% (the model has little data on this, n = 17); the model ignores the resting ECG.
This part reads only ST depression on exercise and acts on 70 of 242 training patients, 50 of whom had heart disease.
Through it, more ST depression adds nothing until about 1.5 mm, then raises the predicted risk steadily: for a typical patient from about 20% at 0 mm to about 45% at 2.8 mm and about 61% at 3.5 mm.
Across the whole model ST depression has the same effect, from about 20% at 0 mm to about 45% at 2.8 mm.

This part reads sex and chest pain on exercise and acts on the 160 of 242 training patients without chest pain on exercise, 47 of whom had heart disease; for the typical patient it acts on, the predicted risk is about 1% both without it and with it.
Through it, being a woman lowers a typical patient's predicted risk from about 20% to about 7%, and chest pain brought on by exercise raises it to about 27%.
Across the whole model, being a woman lowers the risk more when exercise does not bring on chest pain: from about 20% to below 1%, against about 27% to about 1% when it does.

This part reads fasting blood sugar and the thallium scan and acts on the 15 of 242 training patients with a fixed defect on the thallium scan, 9 of whom had heart disease; for the typical patient it acts on, the predicted risk is above 99% without it and about 90% with it (the model has little data on this, n = 15).

Through it, a fixed defect on the thallium scan lowers a typical patient's predicted risk from about 20% to about 1%, but only if fasting blood sugar is 120 mg/dL or less; with fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL it stays at about 3% (the model has little data on this, n = 15).
For the typical patient it acts on, fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL raises the risk through it from about 90% to above 99%.

This part adds more for each vessel coloured by fluoroscopy: through it, a typical patient's predicted risk rises steadily from about 20% at 0 to about 45% at 2 vessels, each extra vessel adding about the same.

Across the whole model, the vessels raise it steadily, each extra vessel adding about the same, from about 20% at 0 to about 99% at 2 vessels, flattening out near the top because the predicted risk cannot go much higher.
Through it, a thallium result coded 4 also raises the risk, to about 93% (the model has little data on this, n = 2).
This part reads only whether the patient has atypical angina and barely changes the predictions: through it, atypical angina takes a typical patient's predicted risk from about 20% to about 19%.

lead.text: For a typical patient (a 56-year-old man with no chest pain symptoms and median test results) the model predicts a risk of heart disease of about 20%; it adds up most of its inputs independently, and five small parts add to that sum: one switches on for the 70 of 242 training patients with marked ST depression on exercise, one acts on the 160 without chest pain on exercise, and three more are explained below.

evidence.text: Through it, a typical patient's predicted risk rises steadily from about 20% at 0 to about 45% at 2 vessels.
Through it, a thallium result coded 4 also raises the risk, to about 93% (the model has little data on this, n = 2).
Its formula reproduces the part exactly on all 242 training patients.

hypothesis.text: This part captures the coronary burden: it weights the number of vessels coloured by fluoroscopy and the rare thallium result coded 4, adds a constant, and passes the sum on unchanged because it never falls below zero.

evidence.text: It acts on the 160 of 242 training patients without chest pain on exercise, 47 of whom had heart disease; for the typical patient it acts on, the predicted risk is about 1% both without it and with it.
Through it, being a woman lowers a typical patient's predicted risk from about 20% to about 7%, and chest pain brought on by exercise raises it to about 27%.
Across the whole model, being a woman lowers the risk from about 20% to below 1% when exercise does not bring on chest pain, against about 27% to about 1% when it does.
Its formula reproduces the part exactly on all 242 training patients.

hypothesis.text: This part lowers the predicted risk for patients without chest pain on exercise, and lowers it most for women without it.

evidence.text: It acts on the 15 of 242 training patients with a fixed defect on the thallium scan, 9 of whom had heart disease; for the typical patient it acts on, the predicted risk is above 99% without it and about 90% with it (the model has little data on this, n = 15).

Through it, a fixed defect on the thallium scan lowers a typical patient's predicted risk from about 20% to about 1% if fasting blood sugar is 120 mg/dL or less, and leaves it at about 3% if fasting blood sugar is above 120 mg/dL (the model has little data on this, n = 15).
For the typical patient it acts on, fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL raises the risk through it from about 90% to above 99%.
Its formula reproduces the part exactly on all 242 training patients.

hypothesis.text: This part lowers the predicted risk for patients with a fixed defect on the thallium scan, but only if their fasting blood sugar is 120 mg/dL or less (the model has little data on this, n = 15).

evidence.text: It acts on 70 of 242 training patients, 50 of whom had heart disease; for the typical patient it acts on, the predicted risk is above 99% both without it and with it.
Through it, more ST depression adds nothing until about 1.5 mm, then raises the risk steadily, for a typical patient from about 20% at 0 mm to about 45% at 2.8 mm and about 61% at 3.5 mm.
Its formula reproduces the part exactly on all 242 training patients.

hypothesis.text: This part raises the predicted risk with ST depression on exercise: nothing until about 1.5 mm, then steadily, but only for patients with a flat ST segment.

evidence.text: Through it, atypical angina takes a typical patient's predicted risk from about 20% to about 19%, and switching it off barely changes the predictions.
Its formula reproduces the part exactly on all 242 training patients.

hypothesis.text: This part reads only whether the patient has atypical angina and barely changes the predictions.

evidence.text: It is made up of the inputs that feed the score directly and five parts, the ST depression hinge, the part for patients without chest pain on exercise, the fixed thallium defect part, the vessel count boost and the atypical angina offset (each explained below); the score is their sum, which was checked on all 242 training patients.
ST depression on exercise and chest pain on exercise do not feed the score directly, so each acts only through its part.

Changing one input at a time across the whole model, each extra vessel takes a typical patient from about 20% at 0 to about 99% at 2 vessels, against about 96% through the sum alone, and being a woman lowers the risk to below 1%, against about 1% through the sum alone.
Across the whole model a fixed defect on the thallium scan lowers it to about 1% and a thallium result coded 4 raises it to about 93% (the model has little data on this, n = 15 and 2).
The model ignores the resting ECG.

hypothesis.text: The model adds up its inputs into one score: the vessels coloured (each extra vessel adding about the same), the ST segment, chest pain type and sex each move the predicted risk on their own, five small parts add to that sum, and the resting ECG is ignored.

parts.name: heart_disease_logit
parts.original_hypothesis: Root: logit z = -0.954 + LINEAR CORE + 1.893*vessel_count_linear_boost - 0.452*sex_exang_protective_gate - 0.942*fbs_normal_fixed_defect_gate + 1.108*oldpeak_hinge - 0.154*cp2_constant_offset; prediction = sigmoid(z) (get_formula shows the output node as ReLU, but the evaluator overrides it with sigmoid for binary classification; compute_performance on train, AUC 0.9437 and acc 0.888, matches sigmoid(z)). LINEAR CORE (standardised inputs): +2.065 ca, +1.665 sex:1, -0.070 sex:0, +1.298 slope:2, -0.499 slope:1, +1.075 chol, -0.972 cp:3, -0.916 cp:1, +0.618 cp:4, -0.057 cp:2, -0.667 fbs:1, +0.616 trestbps, +0.461 thal:7, -0.419 thalach, +0.205 age. Inputs restecg:0/1/2, exang:1, slope:3 and thal:3 are disconnected in the phenotype and enter the root with zero effect. CHILDREN (all additive, read out directly by the output; no serial composition): vessel_count_linear_boost is affine (never clips), raising the effective ca weight to 2.60; sex_exang_protective_gate lowers the logit by 0.43 (men) or 1.67 (women) only when there is no exercise angina; oldpeak_hinge adds 1.11 per SD of ST depression above +0.39 SD (the only oldpeak pathway); fbs_normal_fixed_defect_gate subtracts 3.19 for the 10 training patients with a fixed thallium defect and normal fasting sugar (likely an overfitted correction); cp2_constant_offset is a near-inert -0.044 offset for cp:2. EVIDENCE (train, n=242): the linear core dominates (logit sd 4.96 vs 1.41 for all readouts); with every readout fixed at its mean, train AUC is 0.9295 and accuracy 0.860, vs 0.9437 and 0.888 for the full model. SHAP (probability scale) ranks ca 0.158, sex:1 0.104, slope:2 0.092, cp:3 0.053, chol 0.044, cp:4 0.041. So the network is a logistic regression (more vessels, male sex, flat ST slope, high cholesterol, asymptomatic chest pain mean more risk) with two clinically plausible one-sided terms (marked ST depression adds risk; no exertional angina lowers it, more for women) and one small-sample correction.

parts.name: oldpeak_hinge
parts.original_hypothesis: Node 2985 = ReLU(1.002*oldpeak - 0.386), read out with +1.108. A hinge on exercise-induced ST depression: zero for patients with oldpeak below +0.385 SD (71% of train), then +1.11 logit per SD above it (max +4.41). Disease rate 0.71 where active vs 0.33 where inactive. It is the network's only oldpeak pathway, so the network treats small ST depression as uninformative and only marked depression as risk. Mean-ablation drops train AUC 0.9437 -> 0.9400 and accuracy 0.888 -> 0.876.

parts.name: sex_exang_protective_gate
parts.original_hypothesis: Node 791 = ReLU(0.325 + 1.084*sex:0 - 0.218*sex:1 + 2.200*exang:0), read out with -0.452. Since sex and exang are one-hot binaries it takes only three values on train: 0 for all patients with exercise-induced angina (n=82, disease rate 0.73), 0.959 for men without it (n=96) and 3.702 for women without it (n=64). It is therefore a protective interaction: absence of exertional angina lowers the logit by 0.43 for men but by 1.67 for women, and has no effect if angina is present. This is the network's only exang pathway (no direct exang edge). Readout sd 0.66 logits; mean-ablation drops train AUC 0.9437 -> 0.9418, accuracy unchanged.

parts.name: fbs_normal_fixed_defect_gate
parts.original_hypothesis: Node 2034 = ReLU(-1.027 + 1.156*fbs:0 + 1.016*thal:6), read out with -0.942. An AND gate: it is 3.386 only for patients with a fixed thallium defect (thal:6) AND normal fasting blood sugar (n=10 on train), 0.018 for fixed-defect patients with high sugar (n=5), and 0 for everyone else (93.8%). It subtracts 3.19 logits for that small group. Evidence suggests it is a training-set correction rather than a clinical rule: among the 10, the linear core over-predicted 4 of 5 negatives as positive; the gate moves all 5 negatives below 0 while the 5 positives stay above 0. This is the only thal:6 pathway and the only fbs:0 pathway. Mean-ablation drops train AUC 0.9437 -> 0.9388 and accuracy 0.888 -> 0.872 (largest single-gate effect), but it rests on 10 patients, so treat it as likely overfitted.

confidence_rules.clearly: a meaningful change in predicted risk for a typical patient (at least 5% points), the test split agrees (same sign, and its bootstrap interval over test patients excludes no benefit), and every group has at least 20 training patients
confidence_rules.consistently across patients: the claim holds for at least 90% of training patients (range across patients); this is not a significance statement
confidence_rules.on the training data only: the test split disagrees (opposite sign, or no benefit on test patients) or is unclear (its interval includes no benefit), or no test check is available
confidence_rules.slightly: the change in predicted risk for a typical patient is below 5% points
confidence_rules.the model has little data on this: a compared group has fewer than 20 training patients
